description: I'm a 6th-semester Computer Science student participating independently in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I'm passionate about web development, software engineering, and space exploration. My project focuses on building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer to help students understand the challenges of managing a Moon or Mars mission through an engaging digital experience.
summary: Mission: Mars Frontier is an interactive, browser-based educational game designed for children aged 7–12. Players take on the role of a Mission Commander leading a team of five astronauts on a series of Mars exploration missions. Through interactive scenarios, crew discussions, and decision-making challenges, players experience some of the difficulties involved in establishing and maintaining a human outpost on Mars.
details:
Mission: Mars Frontier

What It Does

Mission: Mars Frontier is an interactive, browser-based educational game designed for children aged 7–12. It allows players to experience the challenges of exploring Mars by taking the role of a Mission Commander responsible for leading a crew of five astronauts. The game introduces young learners to important concepts of human space exploration, including power management, life-support systems, radiation safety, teamwork, and communication challenges.

How It Works

The game takes players through four mission scenarios:

  1. Arrival on Mars: Players begin their journey by establishing a base and making important initial mission decisions.
  2. Power Crisis: A Martian dust storm affects solar power generation, requiring players to make decisions about limited energy resources.
  3. Lost Rover: Players respond to a rover communication problem and work with their crew to handle the situation.
  4. Radiation Alert: Players face a space-weather threat and must consider ways to protect the astronauts.

Players interact with five crew members, each with a different role and expertise. They receive advice, evaluate possible decisions, and experience the consequences of their choices. This makes the experience more engaging than simply reading facts about space exploration.

Benefits and Educational Value

The project helps children understand that space exploration involves real challenges and difficult decisions. It develops critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, teamwork, and curiosity about science. It also introduces children to the responsibilities astronauts may face while living and working on another planet.

Goals and Intended Impact

Our main goal is to make space science accessible, enjoyable, and interactive for young learners. We want to encourage children to explore STEM subjects and develop an interest in astronomy, engineering, and future space missions. By presenting space exploration through missions and storytelling, we aim to turn complex scientific ideas into an experience that children can understand and enjoy.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using web technologies, including:

  • React.js for building the interactive user interface.
  • JavaScript for game logic and interactive functionality.
  • Vite as the development and build tool.
  • HTML and CSS for structure and styling.
  • Tailwind CSS for interface styling.
  • Lucide icons for interface elements.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Mission: Mars Frontier combines educational content with a mission-based gameplay experience. Its Mars-inspired visual environment, fictional astronaut crew, interactive scenarios, and decision-making system help create an engaging learning experience. During development, we considered the target age group, ease of navigation, visual clarity, accessibility, educational value, and the importance of presenting space exploration challenges in a simple and understandable way.
